source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

limiting_factors.detail: relative water-erosion index 0.69 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
mean slope 10.4 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)

annual rainfall 358.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 352.0 mm) vs barley season ET 509.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 60.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) when irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); external water (transfers, fossil groundwater, wastewater) is NOT assumed or mapped

water.basis: TerraClimate 2011-2020 mean annual climatic water surplus (P - AET) at ~4 km, 1 mm = 10 m3/ha; an upper bound on renewable water generated at this location (runoff + recharge), before any capture losses

irrigation.basis: lowest central net irrigation requirement among the irrigated scenarios (best-scoring crop of each), compared with local renewable water

water.not_mapped: groundwater storage and abstraction limits, fossil aquifers, national water transfers, treated wastewater, dams and canals

interventions.name: Microcatchment / contour-bund water harvesting
interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. Rainfall in this region is highly variable (FAO: 100 mm/yr -> 30-350 % of mean), so failure years are expected.
interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 3.7:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 352.0 mm in 2 years out of 3
source_refs: FAO_WH91: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91. <https://www.fao.org/3/u3160e/u3160e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.45 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

limiting_factors.detail: relative water-erosion index 0.71 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
mean slope 9.4 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)

annual rainfall 394.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 386.0 mm) vs barley season ET 503.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 66.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) when irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); external water (transfers, fossil groundwater, wastewater) is NOT assumed or mapped

water.basis: TerraClimate 2011-2020 mean annual climatic water surplus (P - AET) at ~4 km, 1 mm = 10 m3/ha; an upper bound on renewable water generated at this location (runoff + recharge), before any capture losses

irrigation.basis: lowest central net irrigation requirement among the irrigated scenarios (best-scoring crop of each), compared with local renewable water

water.not_mapped: groundwater storage and abstraction limits, fossil aquifers, national water transfers, treated wastewater, dams and canals

interventions.name: Microcatchment / contour-bund water harvesting
interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. Rainfall in this region is highly variable (FAO: 100 mm/yr -> 30-350 % of mean), so failure years are expected.
interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 2.8:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 386.0 mm in 2 years out of 3
source_refs: FAO_WH91: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91. <https://www.fao.org/3/u3160e/u3160e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.09 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.1 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.2 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.0 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 10.1 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 2931.0-4540.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3879.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.1 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.35 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 10.1 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 2923.0-4606.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3776.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.1 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.38 %; improves water holding and infiltration

interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.1 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3117.0-4591.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3845.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.1 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.0 % <= 5 % target)

SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates
TerraClimate 2011-2020 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) - rainfall, ET0
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM - slope
geoBoundaries gbOpen JOR ADM1 (CC BY 2.5) - boundary

limiting_factors.detail: relative water-erosion index 0.71 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
mean slope 11.7 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)

annual rainfall 345.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 336.0 mm) vs barley season ET 506.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 56.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) when irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); external water (transfers, fossil groundwater, wastewater) is NOT assumed or mapped

water.basis: TerraClimate 2011-2020 mean annual climatic water surplus (P - AET) at ~4 km, 1 mm = 10 m3/ha; an upper bound on renewable water generated at this location (runoff + recharge), before any capture losses

irrigation.basis: lowest central net irrigation requirement among the irrigated scenarios (best-scoring crop of each), compared with local renewable water

water.not_mapped: groundwater storage and abstraction limits, fossil aquifers, national water transfers, treated wastewater, dams and canals

interventions.name: Microcatchment / contour-bund water harvesting
interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. Rainfall in this region is highly variable (FAO: 100 mm/yr -> 30-350 % of mean), so failure years are expected.
interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 4.3:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 336.0 mm in 2 years out of 3
source_refs: FAO_WH91: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91. <https://www.fao.org/3/u3160e/u3160e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.97 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Salt/sodicity-tolerant crop selection (date palm, barley, tall wheatgrass, olive)
interventions.description: Choose crops whose Maas-Hoffman threshold exceeds the achievable root-zone ECe (FAO Table 4) and whose ESP class tolerates the residual sodicity.
interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 1.8 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

Rainfall in this region is highly variable (FAO: 100 mm/yr -> 30-350 % of mean), so failure years are expected.
interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 4.3:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 338.0 mm in 2 years out of 3
source_refs: FAO_WH91: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91. <https://www.fao.org/3/u3160e/u3160e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.43 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Salt/sodicity-tolerant crop selection (date palm, barley, tall wheatgrass, olive)
interventions.description: Choose crops whose Maas-Hoffman threshold exceeds the achievable root-zone ECe (FAO Table 4) and whose ESP class tolerates the residual sodicity.
interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 0.6 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

limiting_factors.detail: relative water-erosion index 0.75 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
mean slope 11.0 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)

annual rainfall 368.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 357.0 mm) vs barley season ET 504.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 60.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) when irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); external water (transfers, fossil groundwater, wastewater) is NOT assumed or mapped

water.basis: TerraClimate 2011-2020 mean annual climatic water surplus (P - AET) at ~4 km, 1 mm = 10 m3/ha; an upper bound on renewable water generated at this location (runoff + recharge), before any capture losses

irrigation.basis: lowest central net irrigation requirement among the irrigated scenarios (best-scoring crop of each), compared with local renewable water

water.not_mapped: groundwater storage and abstraction limits, fossil aquifers, national water transfers, treated wastewater, dams and canals

interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 9.9 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 2891.0-4261.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3715.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.2 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.1 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction

interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.8 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Microcatchment / contour-bund water harvesting
interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. Rainfall in this region is highly variable (FAO: 100 mm/yr -> 30-350 % of mean), so failure years are expected.
interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 4.6:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 328.0 mm in 2 years out of 3
source_refs: FAO_WH91: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91. <https://www.fao.org/3/u3160e/u3160e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.4 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Salt/sodicity-tolerant crop selection (date palm, barley, tall wheatgrass, olive)
interventions.description: Choose crops whose Maas-Hoffman threshold exceeds the achievable root-zone ECe (FAO Table 4) and whose ESP class tolerates the residual sodicity.
interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 0.9 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

limiting_factors.detail: relative water-erosion index 0.51 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)

annual rainfall 372.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 357.0 mm) vs barley season ET 505.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 61.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
mean slope 7.4 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) when irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); external water (transfers, fossil groundwater, wastewater) is NOT assumed or mapped

water.basis: TerraClimate 2011-2020 mean annual climatic water surplus (P - AET) at ~4 km, 1 mm = 10 m3/ha; an upper bound on renewable water generated at this location (runoff + recharge), before any capture losses

irrigation.basis: lowest central net irrigation requirement among the irrigated scenarios (best-scoring crop of each), compared with local renewable water

water.not_mapped: groundwater storage and abstraction limits, fossil aquifers, national water transfers, treated wastewater, dams and canals

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3002.0-4579.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3684.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 1.9 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.34 %; improves water holding and infiltration

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction

interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.6 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.8 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching

interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.1 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 11.3 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 2894.0-4230.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3690.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.1 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.12 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.8 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 1.9 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion

interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.8 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.04 %; improves water holding and infiltration

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.3 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 1.0 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

limiting_factors.detail: relative water-erosion index 0.82 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
mean slope 13.1 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)

annual rainfall 440.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 419.0 mm) vs barley season ET 478.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 75.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) when irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); external water (transfers, fossil groundwater, wastewater) is NOT assumed or mapped

water.basis: TerraClimate 2011-2020 mean annual climatic water surplus (P - AET) at ~4 km, 1 mm = 10 m3/ha; an upper bound on renewable water generated at this location (runoff + recharge), before any capture losses

irrigation.basis: lowest central net irrigation requirement among the irrigated scenarios (best-scoring crop of each), compared with local renewable water

water.not_mapped: groundwater storage and abstraction limits, fossil aquifers, national water transfers, treated wastewater, dams and canals

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 13.1 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 2925.0-4441.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3553.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.5 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.7 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.4 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 1.9 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 12.1 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3083.0-4680.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3830.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.9 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.51 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.

interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.9 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 1.8 % <= 5 % target)

SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates
TerraClimate 2011-2020 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) - rainfall, ET0
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM - slope
geoBoundaries gbOpen JOR ADM1 (CC BY 2.5) - boundary

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 263.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 252.0 mm) vs barley season ET 547.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 38.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
mean slope 8.9 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)
relative water-erosion index 0.33 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) when irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); external water (transfers, fossil groundwater, wastewater) is NOT assumed or mapped

water.basis: TerraClimate 2011-2020 mean annual climatic water surplus (P - AET) at ~4 km, 1 mm = 10 m3/ha; an upper bound on renewable water generated at this location (runoff + recharge), before any capture losses

irrigation.basis: lowest central net irrigation requirement among the irrigated scenarios (best-scoring crop of each), compared with local renewable water

water.not_mapped: groundwater storage and abstraction limits, fossil aquifers, national water transfers, treated wastewater, dams and canals

interventions.name: Microcatchment / contour-bund water harvesting
interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. Rainfall in this region is highly variable (FAO: 100 mm/yr -> 30-350 % of mean), so failure years are expected.
interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 7.7:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 252.0 mm in 2 years out of 3
source_refs: FAO_WH91: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91. <https://www.fao.org/3/u3160e/u3160e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.74 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Salt/sodicity-tolerant crop selection (date palm, barley, tall wheatgrass, olive)
interventions.description: Choose crops whose Maas-Hoffman threshold exceeds the achievable root-zone ECe (FAO Table 4) and whose ESP class tolerates the residual sodicity.
interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 2.3 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Rain-fed cultivation with microcatchment water harvesting and mulch/organic amendment
residual_risks: rainfall failure years (annual rain 30-350 % of mean in hyper-arid zones, FAO) and flash-flood damage to bunds
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)

relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)

simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

interventions.name: Microcatchment / contour-bund water harvesting
interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 3.5:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 360.0 mm in 2 years out of 3

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.8 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.3 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.4 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.28 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 12.7 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 2952.0-4375.0 m3/ha/yr (central 3817.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.0 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.14 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)

interventions.description: Concentrates runoff onto the cultivated area: catchment:cultivated ratio C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR K EFF), K 0.1-0.5, EFF 0.5-0.75, design rainfall DR at 67 % exceedance. Rainfall in this region is highly variable (FAO: 100 mm/yr -> 30-350 % of mean), so failure years are expected.
interventions.expected_effect: required catchment:cultivated area ratio about 5.7:1 (limit 6-12:1); rainfall 296.0 mm in 2 years out of 3
source_refs: FAO_WH91: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91. <https://www.fao.org/3/u3160e/u3160e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 2.31 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.7 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching

interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.0 % <= 5 % target)
